documents: Passport plus secondary ID, foreign address proof, and usually an SSN or ITIN; some branches accept passport-only for non-resident aliens with a W-8BEN.
min_deposit_fees: Varies by bank; typical checking accounts have no or low opening deposit and monthly fees of about USD 5-15 unless waived.
banks: Bank of America, Chase, Citibank, PNC, Wells Fargo (branch visit, ITIN accepted by several).
restrictions: Most major banks require an in-person US branch visit; heavy KYC and de-risking of non-residents; W-8BEN and FATCA/CRS reporting apply.
alternatives: Wise USD account details, Revolut, Zolve, Payoneer; Mercury/Relay only for US LLC business accounts.
cost_note: Chase Total Checking: no opening fee or minimum opening deposit, USD 15 monthly service fee (raised from USD 12 in Aug 2025) waivable with USD 500 direct deposits or a USD 1,500 daily balance; already in USD.

documents: Passport (notarised copies if not original), proof of foreign address, bank reference letter from a bank of 3+ years' relationship, source of funds, CRS/FATCA self-certification.
min_deposit_fees: Not published officially; guides cite roughly USD 5,000 for non-residents, older reports far lower.
banks: Bank of Saint Lucia (dedicated non-national/non-resident customer type), 1st National Bank St Lucia, Republic Bank (EC).
restrictions: Strict correspondent-banking KYC; Hermes Bank in liquidation since 2025; XCD pegged to USD.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (no local EC dollar details); citizenship-by-investment holders get easier access.
cost_note: Minimum deposit is the roughly USD 5,000 non-resident figure cited by third-party guides (not an official Bank of Saint Lucia tariff); opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport with valid entry stamp, proof of address, bank reference letters; many banks want a Honduran residency card or RTN tax number.
banks: BAC Credomatic, Banco Ficohsa, Banco Atlantida, Davivienda (case-by-case for non-residents).
restrictions: Banks historically discouraged from opening accounts for foreigners without residency; approval at branch manager discretion; remote opening mainly for Hondurans abroad.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, remittance services (e.g. Western Union).
cost_note: Honduras: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Passport, proof of address (utility bill), proof of income, Guyana TIN certificate, and a banker's reference for foreign nationals.
min_deposit_fees: Republic Bank Guyana savings minimums cited from GYD 5,000 to GYD 100,000 depending on product.
banks: Republic Bank (Guyana) - foreign national accounts subject to conditions.
restrictions: TIN required; Republic's non-resident foreign currency account targets those living abroad; foreign currency scarcity and USD account approvals reported.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; remittance services.
cost_note: Republic Bank (Guyana) savings minimums are cited from GYD 5,000 (about USD 24 at GYD 209/USD) up to GYD 100,000 depending on product; opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport, Korean mobile number in own name, proof of purpose (employment/enrolment) and local address; ARC needed for full services.
min_deposit_fees: No minimum deposit typically; fees not published.
banks: KB Kookmin, Hana Bank, Shinhan, Woori (in branch, mainly for visitors with a clear Korea connection).
restrictions: Accounts without an ARC are often teller-only with no ATM, online banking or overseas transfer for months; must open in person in Korea; anti-fraud limits on new accounts.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; for travellers, prepaid cards such as WOWPASS.
cost_note: Major Korean banks (KB Kookmin, Hana, Shinhan, Woori) typically need no minimum deposit; opening and monthly fees for non-resident accounts are not published.

documents: Passport with valid Vietnamese visa or temporary residence card, local address and phone, work permit or labour contract for many banks.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; usually low or none at major banks.
banks: None known for true non-residents; foreign residents use Vietcombank, Techcombank, HSBC Vietnam, Shinhan Vietnam.
restrictions: Payment-account rules (Circular 17/2024/TT-NHNN) tie foreigners' accounts to visa/residence validity; savings and foreign-currency deposits by non-residents restricted; biometric verification required.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (no local VND details); foreign portfolio investors use special indirect investment capital accounts.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot realistically open a personal account here, so no cost figures apply (all null).

documents: Passport, Fiji TIN letter (compulsory at BSP), Fiji residential address, proof of address, source of funds.
banks: BSP Fiji, ANZ Fiji, Westpac Fiji (case-by-case; Australian bank ties may help).
restrictions: Exchange controls by Reserve Bank of Fiji; non-resident and foreign currency accounts governed by residency definitions; TIN requirement hampers non-residents.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; keep funds with Australian parent banks (ANZ, Westpac).
cost_note: Fiji: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Passport, bank reference, proof of address and a clear local connection; requirements not published.
banks: Bank of the Marshall Islands (domestic; non-resident personal accounts rare).
restrictions: Tiny sector reliant on a single correspondent relationship; strong de-risking; offshore IBCs barred from local accounts; USD is local currency.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut USD details; US bank accounts.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot realistically open a personal account here, so no cost figures apply (all null).

documents: Passport, Tajik TIN, proof of legal stay (visa/registration); foreign documents may need legalisation at a Tajik mission.
banks: Spitamen Bank (states services for residents and non-residents), Amonatbank (requires proof of legal stay).
restrictions: Physical presence expected; currency controls on somoni; correspondent banking constraints and Russia-related sanctions spillover affect transfers.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (no local details); money transfer systems such as Western Union.
cost_note: Tajikistan: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Passport, residence permit, local proof of address, tax number and initial deposit.
banks: None known for non-residents; local banks include BANGE, Societe Generale Equatorial Guinea, CCEI Bank GE, Ecobank.
restrictions: CEMAC/BEAC exchange controls (2018 regulation) tightly restrict foreign-currency accounts and transfers; heavy AML scrutiny.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut not locally available; use home-country accounts and money transfer services.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot realistically open a personal account here, so no cost figures apply (all null).

documents: Passport, reference letter, proof of residence, ZRA TPIN, proof of income; many banks also want a work or study permit.
banks: Stanbic Bank Zambia, Zanaco, Absa Zambia, FNB Zambia (mostly require permits; case-by-case for non-residents).
restrictions: Banks typically ask for a Zambian permit and local address; foreign-currency accounts available but subject to AML checks.
alternatives: Wise, mobile money (MTN MoMo, Airtel Money) once locally registered.
cost_note: Zambia: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Certified passport copy, foreign proof of address (under 3 months), 3 months of foreign bank statements, proof of income, signed bank forms.
min_deposit_fees: Standard Bank non-resident account fees per its pricing guide; 0.60% fee on outward payments outside the CMA; minimum deposit not published.
banks: Standard Bank (dedicated non-resident account, applications by email), FNB, Absa, Nedbank.
restrictions: Exchange control (SARB) rules apply to non-resident rand accounts; FICA KYC; limited credit products for non-residents.
alternatives: Wise ZAR, Revolut; TymeBank/Discovery mainly for residents.
cost_note: Standard Bank's 2026 Non-Residents Pricing Guide was found but its account monthly fee and minimum deposit could not be extracted (it lists outward payments outside the CMA at 0.783%, min ZAR 295.65, max ZAR 991.30, about USD 17-57 at ZAR 17.5/USD), so all three are null.

documents: Two government IDs, proof of foreign address, detailed source of wealth and income, bank references; in-person meeting usually required.
min_deposit_fees: Private banking for non-residents typically EUR 500,000 to EUR 2-3 million; standard accounts cited at EUR 10,000-50,000.
banks: CFM Indosuez, Compagnie Monegasque de Banque, Barclays Monaco, UBS Monaco, Societe Generale Private Banking Monaco.
restrictions: Accounts effectively private-banking only for non-residents; French residents often refused; intensive AML and CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (EU IBANs); French or Luxembourg banks.
cost_note: Minimum deposit is the low end of the EUR 10,000-50,000 cited for standard non-resident accounts (about USD 11,700 at USD 1.17/EUR; private banking needs EUR 500,000+); opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport, foreign proof of address, court-certified translation of foreign documents, purpose of account; some banks want a CIPS residence certificate.
banks: Raiffeisen Bank BiH (non-resident accounts under FBiH rulebook), UniCredit Bank BiH, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH.
restrictions: Non-resident accounts regulated by entity-level rulebooks; documents must be renewed or account is blocked; KM pegged to EUR.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, Paysera.
cost_note: Bosnia & Herzegovina: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Passport (6+ months validity), Bulgarian address, foreign tax ID, proof of income, sometimes reference letter or criminal record; LNCH helps.
min_deposit_fees: KYC/document-review fees reported at EUR 100-500 for non-residents; minimum deposit not published.
banks: UniCredit Bulbank, DSK Bank (power of attorney opening possible case-by-case).
restrictions: Many banks refuse non-EU non-residents without residence permit or D visa; AML/CRS; Bulgaria adopted the euro in 2026.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, Paysera (EU IBANs).
cost_note: Opening fee is the low end of the EUR 100-500 KYC/document-review fees reported for non-residents at UniCredit Bulbank/DSK (about USD 117 at USD 1.17/EUR); minimum deposit and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport, proof of right of residence or residence permit, often personnummer or coordination number, proof of employment or study.
banks: Handelsbanken, SEB, Swedbank, Nordea (rarely for non-residents; limited service without personnummer).
restrictions: Without personnummer, BankID and online banking typically unavailable; strict AML; non-EU non-residents usually refused.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, N26 (EU IBANs; no Swedish BankID).
cost_note: Sweden: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Passport, second ID, foreign proof of address, foreign bank statements, source of funds; FATCA/CRS forms.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; monthly account fees apply and vary by bank.
banks: Bank Leumi, Bank Hapoalim, Mizrahi-Tefahot, Discount Bank (non-resident accounts common for property buyers).
restrictions: Usually requires a branch visit or notarised power of attorney; strict AML and source-of-funds checks; FATCA/CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise ILS, Revolut.
cost_note: Monthly fee is Bank Leumi's cheapest paid plan, Digital Leumi at ILS 10/month (plans range ILS 10-35; about USD 2.7 at ILS 3.7/USD), not confirmed for non-resident accounts; opening fee and minimum deposit are not published.

documents: Passport, foreign proof of address, bank reference letter, proof of income, photo, initial deposit.
banks: Bank Muscat (dedicated non-resident savings accounts, first account in OMR).
restrictions: Non-resident products limited to savings accounts at few banks; branch visit required; AML checks.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (no local OMR details).
cost_note: Bank Muscat needs no minimum to open a savings account but charges a monthly ledger fee if the daily balance falls below OMR 100 (about USD 260 at USD 2.60/OMR); the fee amount and any opening fee are not published in the sources found.

documents: Passport and proof of foreign residence; banks may request extra KYC documents.
banks: Bank of Africa, Attijariwafa Bank, BMCE/CIH, Societe Generale Maroc (convertible-dirham and foreign-currency accounts).
restrictions: Non-residents limited to convertible-dirham or foreign-currency accounts funded only from abroad; Office des Changes exchange controls.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (no MAD local details).
cost_note: Morocco: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

documents: Passport, proof of address, proof of income, notarised documents; banks usually want a GOP or residence permit.
min_deposit_fees: Not published officially; one guide cites about USD 35,000 minimum balance at Absa Seychelles for non-residents.
banks: Absa Bank Seychelles (reported to accept non-residents with notarised documents).
restrictions: Banks require proof of economic link; strong de-risking of offshore clients; residence/work permit usually required.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; Mauritius or Dubai banks.
cost_note: Minimum balance is the roughly USD 35,000 for non-residents at Absa Seychelles cited by one third-party guide, not an official tariff; opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport and supporting KYC documents submitted digitally; no work permit needed for MIB non-resident accounts.
min_deposit_fees: MIB non-resident foreigner account: USD 100 annual fee.
banks: Maldives Islamic Bank (Non-Resident Foreigners Deposit Account, USD only).
restrictions: Non-resident accounts USD-only; most banks including Bank of Maldives require a valid visa or work permit.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (no MVR local details).
cost_note: MIB Non-Resident Foreigners Deposit Account charges USD 100 a year (shown as USD 8.33/month); opening fee and current minimum deposit are not published (the USD 100-250 minimums dated from MIB's 2011 launch).

documents: Passport, local address, residence or professional link to the country; requirements not published.
banks: None known for non-residents; local banks include Ecobank Guine-Bissau, Orabank, Banco da Uniao.
restrictions: BCEAO/WAEMU exchange controls; 2026 non-resident CFA account rule covers only WAEMU citizens abroad; very low banking penetration.
alternatives: Mobile money (Orange Money) once locally registered; Wise not available locally.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot realistically open a personal account here, so no cost figures apply (all null).

documents: Passport, proof of address (lease or residential proof), purpose of account; branch presence required.
banks: ProCredit Bank Kosovo, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, TEB Bank (case-by-case for foreign non-residents).
restrictions: Banks expect a branch visit with proof of address; online opening aimed at Kosovo diaspora; euro is local currency; Serbian dinar banking curtailed since 2024.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, Paysera (EUR IBANs).
cost_note: Kosovo: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.
